title: Adaptive CI perf sentinel: context-aware p95 and tokens/sec gating
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement an adaptive CI-side performance validator that compares PR-run throughput (tokens/sec) and latency p95 to an elastic baseline that is context-aware (model size, sequence length distribution, quantization profile). The goal is to reduce false positives for perf regressions while maintaining high sensitivity to real degradations. This ticket covers the core algorithm, CI integration, dashboarding hooks, and a rollout plan for PR gating. The validator should run as part of the PR perf job, emit structured metrics, and return a pass/fail gate decision with a short human-readable summary for annotations.
implementation_notes: Baseline model: maintain a rolling median+MAD window per model-variant (model+quantization+hw-class) with tunable decay; bucket by seq-length bands (0-128,129-512,513-2048,>2048).
For tokens/sec use bootstrapped confidence intervals to estimate expected mean and variance; for latency use quantile smoothing for p95 with exponential decay to avoid transient spikes causing gates.
PR run: collect N=30 microbursts (short synthetic requests) and 10 long-seq samples where applicable; annotate samples with hw-tag and run config.
Incorporate sequence-length weighting: compute weighted p95 that reflects distribution observed in production traces (configurable per project).
Provide a lightweight emulation mode that runs in parallel to current gating to gather signals without blocking (two-week shadowing before enabling hard blocks).
Add a failure explanation payload: top contributing slices (e.g., model variant + seq band) and delta vs baseline for tokens/sec and p95.
Implement in Go as a single executable used by CI perf job; outputs JSON result to stdout and sets exit code 0/1 depending on gate outcome.
acceptance_criteria: CI job correctly computes baseline and compares PR sample; PR with a known +15% p95 regression is flagged in testing harness.
False positive rate on a 2-week shadow run against ~200 PRs is <= 3% (empirically measured).
Gate emits structured JSON with fields: baseline_window, sample_summary, decision, slices_failed (if any), and diagnostic_links.
Dashboard shows per-model rolling baseline and PR deltas; alerts fire when CI gate failure rate exceeds threshold.
Manual override / bypass token is respected by branch protection rules and recorded in gate metadata.
test_plan: Unit tests for baseline aggregator, quantile smoothing, and bootstrapped CI computation.
Synthetic regression injection: create small PRs that change scheduling/packing to induce ~10-30% tokens/sec regressions and verify detection.
Shadow run for 2 weeks across canary projects (search and embeddings teams) to collect false positive statistics.
End-to-end PR job run: include kernel selection variation and quantized model variants to validate slice bucketing.
Backfill historical data from perf-housekeeping bucket to validate baseline stability and warmup behaviour.
gating_logic: Compute per-slice baseline median and MAD over last 30 days or last 500 samples (whichever is smaller).
For tokens/sec: if observed mean < baseline_mean - 3 * bootstrap_se -> fail slice.
For p95: if observed p95 > baseline_p95 + max(absolute_delta_threshold, k * MAD) -> fail slice. k defaults to 3.
Aggregate slice failures weighted by production traffic fraction; fail PR if weighted-failure-score > 0.25 (configurable).
Apply a cooldown suppression window for flakes: a single failing PR won't permanently adjust baseline; require 3 consecutive failing PRs for baseline shift suggestion.
When in shadow mode, log decisions and send metrics but do not block merge.
dependencies: ENG-332110 (PR gating continuous burst synthesis harness) - needs compat with sample format
ENG-63421 (streaming-token-flow-shepherd) - ingestion hooks for tokens/sec aggregation
infra/ci-builders: image with CUDA runtime for microburst synthetic runner
risks: Overfitting baselines to CI synthetic workloads leading to missed regressions on production traffic distribution.
Small sample sizes for large-sequence workloads may reduce statistical power; fallback to conservative thresholds for rare slices.
Increased CI runtime due to extensive sampling; may require parallelization or limits on sample count per job.
Operator confusion if gate emits overly terse explanations; mitigate with clear failure payloads and dashboard drilldowns.
